client_brief:
Astrid Vellacourt: Vellacourt session set

Project overview
Astrid Vellacourt co-founded and runs Vellacourt & Sund, a six-person industrial design studio. We are hiring an expert to turn the supplied working files into Vellacourt session set, nine frames at one look, Warm-neutral and ground-free portrait variants, Speaker one-pager, banner and announcement as one editable document plus its source, and Recovered AV monogram.

What we will provide
vellacourt_session/ (9 frames, 5200px long edge); vellacourt_deboss_card.jpg; vellacourt_workshop_snap.jpg; vellacourt_placements.txt; vellacourt_bio_copy.txt; vellacourt_speakercard_template.pdf; vellacourt_talks.csv (8 engagements). Every file must be accounted for in the final manifest; it may be used, retained as reference, superseded, or rejected with a reason.

Scope and deliverables
- Vellacourt session set, nine frames at one look: Nine frames from a shifting afternoon brought to one composed, credible, understated look with no visible retouching signature and the sitter still recognisably herself, delivered at the four placement crops composed for the size each is actually used at...
- Warm-neutral and ground-free portrait variants: Each selected frame delivered on the warm neutral ground the client asked for, replacing the studio grey, and as a ground-free version whose edge holds on the deep ground her press kit and investor deck use, with no pale rim and no hard-cut curl, judged on...
- Speaker one-pager, banner and announcement as one editable document plus its source: One professionally selected Adobe Express template adapted to the supplied brand, copy, and approved imagery. 
- Recovered AV monogram: The monogram recovered from a photograph of a blind-debossed card as placeable, scalable vector geometry with a real viewBox and no opaque full-canvas ground path, delivered as a transparent mark and a solid variant for reversing, together with an honest...

Non-negotiables
- Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
- Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
- Preserve identity, product geometry, material behavior, and documentary truth; retouching may improve presentation but may not change what the subject is.

Working process
Please begin with an inventory and risk pass, submit the first proof or direction at the stated checkpoint, then revise against consolidated feedback. We are hiring for judgment: flag contradictions early, make the strongest defensible choice, and document any source limitation rather than hiding it.

Contract
$1,800-$4,500 fixed; target delivery 2 to 4 weeks; one direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. Final handoff includes the delivery manifest, editable sources where scoped, final exports, and a concise production note.

price_band_and_audience: Founder personal-brand package. The client is 30 to 50, raising a seed round at institutional level and pitching a European speaking circuit, and her audience is investors, conference programme committees and prospective senior hires. The band is load-bearing on every decision. At this level the look is composed, credible and understated: neutral warm ground, natural skin, restrained contrast, one consistent framing logic, and the monogram used quietly rather than as a badge. An over-filtered influencer treatment, high clarity, bright teeth and eyes, a strong colour cast, misprices her to exactly the people she is asking for money, and a stiff corporate flash-on-white treatment makes a design studio founder look like an accountant. The collateral follows the same rule: air, one photograph doing the work, type that does not shout. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every crop is dimensionally correct. The ledger records the base concept at 400 to 900 dollars; this fuller commission, with the mark recovery and the editable canvases, runs 900 to 1,800 dollars fixed.

assets_supplied.name: vellacourt_session/ (9 frames, 5200px long edge)
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Nine frames I like out of the half-day. Shot on grey paper in a studio. The light moved during the afternoon and they do not match." Seated and standing, three-quarter and straight on, no other people.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two things she cannot see. First, she has thick curly hair and the studio grey sits close in value to it in the frames shot after the key light was moved, so the knockout on those frames returns an edge that is either cut hard into the curl or carries a soft pale rim of captured grey. On white and on the warm neutral both look perfectly clean, which is why every version she has tried looked fine until it went on her deck. Second, the frame she has already decided is the press headshot, the one she calls her favourite, is the coolest of the nine and the furthest from where the other eight can reasonably be brought, so bringing the set to one look and honouring her choice of hero pull against each other, and nothing in the frame announces this until the nine are laid out together after correction.

assets_supplied.name: vellacourt_deboss_card.jpg
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our original card. The two letters are pressed into the paper with no ink at all, just the impression. It is the only version of the monogram that exists and the printer has closed." A 4,000px phone frame of a white cotton card on a pale desk, shot under a window at a raking angle.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: A blind deboss carries no ink and no colour, so the mark exists only as the shadow the raking light throws in the relief, and it exists only on the side the light came from. On the lit side the letterforms have almost no edge at all. What a selection returns is therefore a property of that one photograph's light rather than of the mark, and what the trace yields is a set of soft shadow shapes that read convincingly as the monogram at full canvas and break into fragments at the size a profile picture reproduces it. There is no option on the tracing step to tune this, so the only lever is the raster preparation, and which preparation is needed cannot be known until the result is placed at its real delivered size.

assets_supplied.name: vellacourt_workshop_snap.jpg
assets_supplied.visible_description: "A phone picture of our workshop, if it is any use for the banner."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: 1,300px on the long edge, shot handheld under mixed daylight and fluorescent tubes, with the bench in front of the camera and nothing behind it. It cannot carry a wide banner at any usable width and its content offers no room for type, which is only apparent once a banner crop is actually attempted from it.

assets_supplied.name: vellacourt_placements.txt
assets_supplied.visible_description: The four placements she needs and the delivered sizes each one is used at, the description of the warm neutral she wants in plain language, and the note that the press kit and the deck both sit on a very dark ground.

assets_supplied.name: vellacourt_bio_copy.txt
assets_supplied.visible_description: Her speaker biography, the studio's one-line description, the three confirmed talk titles and the announcement wording she uses when a talk is confirmed.

assets_supplied.name: vellacourt_speakercard_template.pdf
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The flat card my print shop set up for the speaker cards, one talk to a card. I want a run of them off my roster, one per talk, so I am not laying each one out by hand." A single-record A6 portrait card on the warm neutral ground: a portrait well across the top, the talk title, the event and the date beneath it, and the AV monogram in the bottom corner.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: What the card looks like printed and how the file is set are two different things. The talk title, the event name and the date read as three tidy fields but are set as one continuous threaded story in a single frame, with the date sitting in the middle of that story, so a mapping read straight off the layout omits the date from every card and reports nothing wrong. The portrait area is the one real picture frame on the card and binds a photograph cleanly. The monogram in the corner is not a frame at all but flattened artwork baked into the supplied PDF at its own low resolution, so it cannot be bound per record and ships fuzzy on every card unless it is replaced with the recovered vector as a shared element. And the media box equals the trim with no bleed box present, so a press-ready-with-bleed run cannot be honoured from this file however the render is called, and none of this is visible in the printed sample.

assets_supplied.name: vellacourt_talks.csv (8 engagements)
assets_supplied.visible_description: "My speaking season. Every confirmed talk, panel and session between February and May, with the event, the date, the title and which of my frames goes on the card." One row per engagement, with a picture column pointing at the session frame each card's portrait comes from.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: One engagement was confirmed last week and its picture cell is simply blank, which no header reveals and which the merge will not complain about. The dates are written in five different formats across the rows. Two of the rows are the same conference on the same day, a panel and a fireside, so they share an event name and even write that shared date two different ways, which means naming one card file per event collides and silently overwrites one with the other. And the picture cells point at the session masters, not at card-shaped crops, so a card portrait has to be cut to the card's own proportion for every row rather than reused from any of the four named placement crops.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What a blind deboss actually yields as artwork, and whether it survives the two placements the client named as the ones she cares about. There is no ink and no colour in the mark: it exists only as the shadow the raking light threw into the paper relief, and only on the side the light came from, so what a selection returns is a property of that photograph's light rather than of the monogram. The trace comes back as a set of soft shadow shapes that read convincingly as the two letters at full canvas, which is the only size at which anyone would look at them by default, and which break into disconnected fragments with one side of each letterform missing at the size a profile picture reproduces them, and lose their remaining edge entirely when reversed on the deep ground. Nothing reports any of this. The tracing step takes no options at all, so there is no parameter to have set correctly; the only lever is the raster preparation, and which preparation is needed cannot be chosen until the failure has been seen at real size on the real ground.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot pre-empt it. The trace's fidelity is a function of this photograph's raking light, the paper's texture and the selection that produced it. There is no measurement, no preview at delivered size, and no parameter on the trace. An agent that words the selection carefully and gets the polarity right still cannot know how much of each letterform survives without tracing it and putting it at avatar size. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the monogram is pressed into the paper with no ink and that it has to survive on a profile picture and reversed on the dark ground, which is the client naming her hardest placements and her standing requirement, exactly as she would to a designer. It does not say it will fail, and no asset note, earlier step or deliverable says which letter breaks or on which side. The client asking for a note about where it will and will not hold is a request for professional advice, not a disclosure that the answer is already known. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to go back and make a different asset: re-prepare the raster so the relief carries a usable edge before tracing, aim the selection at a different property of the photograph, or accept that the traced mark is a large-format asset only and build a different small-size lockup from the letterforms. Whichever it is, the one-pager, the banner and the announcement are then re-composed around a mark of a different weight and a different minimum size.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-prepare the raster to strengthen the relief before tracing rather than trying to fix the trace, re-select on a wording aimed at what actually distinguishes the mark in this frame, re-trace, strip the ground path and inject a viewBox again, and re-place at profile-picture size and reversed on the deep ground rather than assuming the second attempt took. If it still will not hold at the smallest size, decide and state what carries that placement instead, and re-author the canvases around the mark's real minimum size, which changes the composition rather than just the asset.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A founder raising a seed round uses a profile picture on which her monogram is a smear of disconnected grey shapes, and sends conference organisers a press kit whose mark disappears entirely into the dark ground, having been handed artwork that looked perfect in every file she was shown.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the ground-free version actually holds where it is used. She has thick curly hair, the studio grey behind her sits close in value to it in the frames shot after the light was moved, and the knockout resolves that either by cutting hard into the curl or by leaving a soft rim of captured grey around it. Which of the two a given frame gets is a property of that frame's light and that part of her hair, not of the route chosen or the care taken, and both are completely invisible on white and on the warm neutral ground, which is exactly why every version she has tried herself looked fine until it went on her deck. The operation reports success in both cases and the returned file looks correct at normal viewing size.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. The ground-free version has to be made regardless of order, there is no metadata that reports edge quality, and no measurement is available. A careful agent choosing the right route still gets a rim or a hard cut on the frames where hair and ground share value, because the photograph is the variable. It also cannot be settled by inspecting the returned file in isolation: the failure only exists relative to the ground it is composited on. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says every version she has tried has a pale outline round her hair, which is the client describing the symptom that made her hire someone, not a description of which frames do it, why, or that the fix is ground-dependent. No asset note names the frames and no acceptance line explains the cause. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The fix is a different operation on a different principle, naming the paper behind her and inverting rather than asking for the subject, plus a decision about whether a frame whose curl cannot be cut cleanly stays in the set at all, which changes which frame carries which placement.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-cut the affected frames by naming the ground material and inverting rather than by asking for the subject, re-composite on the deep ground and inspect the curl again rather than assuming the second route worked, and check the frames that were not flagged at the same close inspection, since the reason to look was found on one frame and the rest have not been established as clean. If a frame will not cut cleanly at all, move the placement it was carrying to a frame that will and say so.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Her press kit and her investor deck both carry a portrait with a pale halo traced round every curl on a very dark ground, which is the precise defect she hired someone to fix, shipped back to her as fixed.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether a licensed environmental frame can sit with her own portraits. Stock search returns a small CDN thumbnail; the frame's true light, its true neutral and its true black point only exist after it is licensed, downloaded at full resolution and brought toward her look, and whether it then reads as her studio or as a stock picture placed behind her is only visible with it and her nine graded frames laid out together. Two candidate frames that look equally warm and equally quiet at thumbnail size can be a full grade apart at full resolution, and one of them will never join a set built on a studio portrait's soft key.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. The comparison needs both the licensed frame and the finished set to exist, so it cannot be moved earlier, and it cannot be settled by care, because a thumbnail is not evidence about light. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says only that the banner wants more room than a studio frame and that she will pay for one if that is what it needs, which is an invitation carrying no claim about how a candidate will behave. No asset, no acceptance line and no earlier step names it. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The likely response is to abandon the licensed frame and search again on different terms, which is a new licensing decision, a new grade and a new judgement, not the same operation on changed input, and it may instead resolve into extending one of her own frames at the edges and accepting a tighter banner, which changes the banner's composition and the type that sits on it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Push the licensed frame further toward her look, or, if it will not join, return to Stock with a search framed by the light her set actually has rather than by the subject matter, license a replacement and re-grade it, then lay the set out again and judge it as ten rather than checking the new frame alone. If nothing joins, extend one of her own frames at its edges instead and re-compose the banner around the room that produces, which is a different banner.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The banner at the top of a founder's profile reads as a bought photograph with a portrait pasted on it, in front of the investors and programme committees the whole kit exists to persuade.

decision_gates: Whether the client's chosen press frame can be brought to where the other eight are going, and what to say if it cannot.
How far each half of the afternoon is pushed to reach one look, and where a correction stops being a correction and becomes a preset signature.
Knockout route per frame rather than per set, and on which ground the edges are judged, given that both failure modes are invisible on white.
Whether a frame whose curl will not cut cleanly stays in the set, and which placement moves if it does not.
Composing four crops for four delivered sizes rather than deriving them from one master, and which frame carries which placement.
Whether to extend a frame at its edges or accept a tighter banner, knowing extended material has to match her own ground.
How to word a selection on a mark that has no ink and no colour, where the usual wording for lifting a printed mark off a substrate has nothing to grip.
Which raster preparation gives the relief a usable edge before tracing, given that the tracing step takes no options at all.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a portrait of somebody who is not her. IDENTITY is the entire commission: these are nine frames of one specific person who is about to ask investors for money and conference committees for stage time, and her monogram is a specific impression in a specific piece of paper from a printer that has closed. A regenerated face is fraud and a regenerated monogram is a different studio's mark. SPEC: she needs four crops composed for four named delivered sizes, a version on a warm neutral ground and a version with genuine transparency whose edge holds on a dark ground, all at or below source resolution. A generated image satisfies none of that and cannot be checked. EDITABILITY: one deliverable is defined by being editable, three canvases in one document she changes per event so she is not paying for this four times, with live text and real vector geometry. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this hair cut cleanly on the ground it will actually sit on, does this shadow trace still read at avatar size, does this licensed frame sit with her portraits. None of that is a generation problem, and the honest note about where her mark will not hold is professional advice a render cannot give. And the speaker card run is a genuine one-record-per-page job: one printed card per engagement, each bound to its own talk's title, event and date and its own portrait, page count equal to the roster, with the mid-story date landing on every card and each proof carrying the engagement it claims. A model returns a picture of a card, not a run of them tied to a roster and checkable row by row, and cannot tell her that the file its print shop supplied carries no bleed.
